statewide_places.name: Aiyanar village guardian shrines, statewide
statewide_places.religion: Indigenous, folk and local religious traditions
statewide_places.why_famous: Aiyanar shrines are widespread across Tamil villages, often with terracotta horses and figures offered by devotees; the shrine forms vary by locality.

statewide_places.name: Kal Vittukal (memorial and hero stones), statewide category
statewide_places.religion: Indigenous and folk traditions (ancestor and hero veneration)
statewide_places.why_famous: Memorial stones (nadukal, virakkal, or hero stones) are carved slabs that commemorate warriors, cattle-raiders, or people who died in battle or in community events. The earliest forms are referred to in Sangam-era Tamil literature, and many medieval examples carry inscriptions and carved scenes showing the death, the hero's ascent, and sometimes the wife's sati or family members.
